subject: Runtime routing, subprocessor chain, and erasure timeline — prospect Q&A
messages:
From: Alexandra Green <alex.green@healthnexus.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthnexus.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runtime routing & deletion commitments — a few clarifying Qs

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday — HealthNexus is very interested in Redwood but procurement asked for a short Q&A to finish our internal review. Can you confirm a few specifics so we can move this to legal?

1) Where are LLM requests executed by default (region(s)) and what happens if our tenant pins to EU-only?
2) Which subprocessors are involved in the runtime path (model execution, object storage, telemetry/metrics, caching)? Please call out any possible US-to-EU or EU-to-US hops.
3) If we request data deletion (customer-initiated erasure of request payloads + derived cache + logs), what are the SLAs and what evidence do you provide?

If it's easier, we can take a short 30-min call but a written response is ideal for the audit packet.

Thanks — Alex
Alexandra Green
Director, Cloud Integrations
HealthNexus

On Wed, Apr 21, 2027 at 9:12 AM Alexandra Green <alex.green@healthnexus.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday — HealthNexus is very interested in Redwood but procurement asked for a short Q&A to finish our internal review. Can you confirm a few specifics so we can move this to legal?
>
> 1) Where are LLM requests executed by default (region(s)) and what happens if our tenant pins to EU-only?
> 2) Which subprocessors are involved in the runtime path (model execution, object storage, telemetry/metrics, caching)? Please call out any possible US-to-EU or EU-to-US hops.
> 3) If we request data deletion (customer-initiated erasure of request payloads + derived cache + logs), what are the SLAs and what evidence do you provide?

Hi Alex — appreciate the clear questions. Below is a concise mapping and the evidence we can provide. I attached a lightweight diagram (processing_handoffs_diagram.pdf) and the subprocessor inventory CSV for your record.

1) Execution geography (high level)
- Default (hosted): requests are executed in the region closest to the API endpoint you call (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1). We advertise region in the API and routing is latency-first unless you set a policy.
- EU-only pin: for customers with a residency requirement we support model routing to eu-west1 exclusively (no cross-region execution) when you select the "EU processing" option. That option pins both the model runtime and short-lived KV caches to EU infrastructure.
- Fallbacks: if you opt-in to cross-region fallbacks (not recommended for strict residency), there is an automated fallback path to compatible model variants in other regions; we flag those in the audit logs when triggered.

2) Subprocessor and hop summary (runtime path)
- Model execution: GCP (Compute) in the chosen region (we also support dedicated pools on partner infra for Dedicated customers).
- Object storage (artifacts, model weights): GCS (regional buckets) or customer-managed object stores for Private/Dedicated deployments.
- KV cache / prefix cache: Redis-compatible cache (CacheCorp) deployed regionally; caches are ephemeral and colocated with the runtime when EU pin is used.
- Telemetry / metrics: internal observability pipelines use MetricsStream (third-party) with regional aggregation — telemetry events are sliced by region; aggregated telemetry may be stored in a US analytics tenant for platform-wide trends (we can opt to exclude customer identifiers from that aggregate).
- Audit logs / request logs: retained at the region for 30 days by default; aggregated backups may reside in a central logging store (us-central) for durability — we can provide an export/attestation for EU pinned customers.

Cross-border hops to call out:
- For hosted accounts without region pins, requests can start in EU then hit model shards in a US region if model variant selection triggers cross-region routing (we surface these events).
- With EU pin enabled there are no EU->US runtime hops for request execution or KV cache.

3) Deletion / erasure SLAs and evidence
- KV/prefix cache: cleared immediately on erasure request; background tombstone/compaction finalized within 1 hour.
- Request payloads & derived artifacts: by default we retain request payloads for 30 days to support debugging; on erasure request we remove payloads from active stores within 24 hours and purge backups within 30 days.
- Audit and access logs: standard retention 90 days; we can configure reduced retention (30/7 days) for dedicated customers per contract.
- Evidence we provide: a signed deletion confirmation (PDF) with timestamps, an exported subprocessor log lines showing affected storage objects, and a short report describing which services/regions were touched. We can also provide GCP export IDs and a Drive link to the artifact.

Next steps / offer
- I've attached the diagram and inventory. If you confirm you want EU-only processing we will prepare a short annex with the residency commitment and adjusted retention SLAs for the deal (RF-2027-1834).

Attachments: processing_handoffs_diagram.pdf, subprocessor_inventory.csv

If you want, I can set a 20-min call with Marissa (contracts) to align the annex language and DocuSign flow.

Best,

Alexandra — looping in procurement support.

Thanks for the quick review. We can include the residency and deletion commitments as a one-page annex to the master services agreement. Key points we'll propose:
- EU Processing Annex: runtime and KV cache pinned to eu-west1; no cross-border runtime hops permitted.
- Erasure SLA: active store purge within 24 hours; final backup purge within 30 days; immediate cache purge and tombstone complete within 1 hour.
- Subprocessor attestation: we will attach the signed subprocessor inventory and provide a timestamped export showing the objects impacted by any erasure.

I will draft the annex and send a DocuSign link by end of day for your legal to review. If HealthNexus needs a shorter backup purge window (e.g., 7 days) we can discuss commercial terms in the quote.
